title: Spot the AI
about: Tell apps that follow a recipe from AI that learned from examples.

cards.prompt: Your phone learned your face. These two robots sort fruit — how did **Robot B** get good at spotting apples?

image.alt: Two robots sorting a red apple. Robot A holds a recipe card reading red plus round equals apple. Robot B has a stack of apple photos. Both robots say apple.

options.text: By seeing lots of apple photos
A person wrote it a recipe
options.nudge: That's **Robot A** — it holds the recipe card. **Robot B** has a stack of photos it learned from.

cards.hint: Look at what each robot is holding. Robot A has a recipe card. What is Robot B holding?
cards.explanation: Yes! Robot B learned from **photos**. Now watch this…

image.alt: The same two robots, now with a green apple between them. Neither has answered yet.
image.revealAlt: Robot A says not apple (wrong). Robot B says apple (right).

options.nudge: Robot A's recipe only knows *red*. A green apple isn't red.
Robot A's recipe only knows *red* — a green apple breaks it.
Robot B saw green apples in its photos, so it still gets it.

cards.hint: Robot A's recipe says *red*. Is a green apple red?
cards.explanation: Robot A's recipe only knew *red*, so it misses the green apple. Robot B learned from examples — it still gets it.

cards.title: Recipe, or learned from examples?
cards.body:
**Robot A follows a recipe** a person wrote: *red + round = apple*. A **calculator** does too. It breaks on anything new.

**Robot B learned from examples** — lots of photos — so it copes with new ones. Your **spam filter** learned the same way. That's **AI**.

cards.prompt: Which **follow a recipe**, and which **learned from examples**?
cards.hint: Could a person write down the exact steps? Then it follows a recipe. If it had to learn from lots of cases, it learned from examples.
cards.nudge: A recipe does the same exact steps every time. Learning from examples copes with new cases nobody wrote down.
cards.explanation: A **calculator**, **timed lights** and an **alarm** follow a recipe. A **spam filter**, **video picks** and **face unlock** learned from examples — too many emails, videos and faces for a recipe.

cards.prompt: A red **ball** rolls in. Who gets it right?

image.alt: The same two robots, now with a red ball between them. Neither has answered yet.
image.revealAlt: Robot A says apple (wrong). Robot B says not apple (right).

options.nudge: Its recipe is just *red + round* — and a ball is both. So the recipe is fooled.
Red and round fools Robot A's recipe. It calls the ball an apple.
Robot B learned what apples really look like, so it isn't fooled.

cards.hint: Robot A's recipe is just *red + round*. A ball is red and round too…
cards.explanation: A red ball is red and round, so Robot A's recipe says *apple* — wrong! Robot B learned what apples really look like, so it isn't fooled.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- **Follows a recipe:** exact steps a person wrote (a calculator).
- **Learned from examples:** got good from lots of cases, so it copes with new ones. That's **AI** (face unlock).

**Try this:** find an app that gets better the more you use it — like video picks. It learned from examples.

Next: teach a robot yourself, and watch it slip up.
